notes.title: Dino Trauma DevBlog #7: Roadmap Update
notes.notes:
[p]Hello friends!  

2025 is shaping up to be a huge year for Dino Trauma. We’ve been working hard behind the scenes, cooking up new content, improving core systems, and making sure every update hits harder than the last. With ambitious goals ahead, exciting changes are on the horizon…
[/p][p]So, let’s take a look at the updated roadmap:  

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43155973/4d3a262b374a8f58c12edc3b76378169ee6814e6.png"][/img][/p][p]Originally, we planned to launch Episode 2 in early 2025, right after Expedition Mode. However, after our first internal playtests, we weren’t satisfied with the quality. The overall flow and level design needed a major overhaul. Additionally, Episode 2 turned out to be so large that we decided to split it into two parts! Part 1 will arrive sooner, while Part 2 will get the extra time it deserves to be truly outstanding.   [/p][p][/p][p]We also want to take a moment to remind you that this project is created by just two people working after hours (a married couple). So please, recommend us to your friends, leave reviews, give us a feedback and support the game by purchasing it ([b]now 33% off[/b]). Every single copy matters and helps us move forward faster toward version 1.0.[/p][p][/p][p]Here’s a few screenshots:   [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43155973/8fae6c7fd2ac5c4a6dc23c8ac0c3766aeb8d9376.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43155973/e723dc551318ec2dd940df6951db788cfa07e28a.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43155973/5b63e50877335353e9a432f62aaff729063f4762.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43155973/316f9364f5b8a5a9ef43ff286f7e52aa82ed0361.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43155973/8542179b614d7ed74c5b3001b44e2dc0a56fa19f.png"][/img]

From our hearts to yours,  [/p][p]thank you for being part of this journey! [/p][p][/p][p]Łukasz & Anastasiia

notes.title: [0.4.904] Expedtion Mode Patch Release
notes.notes:
Happy Holidays, Dino Fans! 

This update brings some new features to Dino Trauma while also laying the ground work for future updates. From new game mode and enemies, to many improvements and fixes.

[h2]Expedition Mode[/h2]

Expeditions are optional activities during which you go to Abandoned Area and face incredibly strong opponents. These expeditions can be compared to raids - Agent Grant moves to a location with strong enemies and has to complete all the objectives within a time limit.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43155973/fe81dce86d294f60d2f0a49b6b35fc6d9671e165.png[/img]

[h2]Crisis Monitor[/h2]

Crisis Monitor unlocks expedtion and makes story levels more unpredictable. Some content will be locked for you until you increase your Crisis Level (higher expedition tiers).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43155973/1308e2e4b646f2fdad4403e6d75699bbd76e962b.png[/img]

[h2]Inventory[/h2]

From now In Dino Trauma you have several items that can be bought, found or aquired. Those items serve different purposes from opening chests, doors, increasing crisis etc. Also we added Agent Grant avatar with visualisation of currently used gear.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43155973/0c6d13c5c26c3c001aabb4d6d0121464d33e659d.png[/img]

[h2]Is the game dead?[/h2]

Nope! Honestly, it's not surprising that many people thought Dino Trauma was inactive given how little we've posted here. But I want to reassure everyone that it's very much still alive. Progress on the game has been slow, though, especially until recently. It's a two-person project (just me and my wife—who I married a few months ago, yay! ❤️). Since I'm working full-time as a Unity Developer for another studio, the only time we can focus on Dino Trauma is during my off-hours or when life gives us a break.

However, Episode 2 is about 70% complete! There's still some work left to get it to a point we're happy with, but... fingers crossed guys. I think it won't be too long 😊.

notes.title: A massive "Thanks" from all of us behind Dino Trauma! ❤️
notes.notes:
Hey Dino Fans!

Thank you all for supporting our little project. Today is one year after the beginning of Early Access, but when Anastasiia and myself (Lukasz) started development, we never expected this... We're just two people making our first game, so it means a lot to see the community and fans love it.

We're still putting in a lot of effort to add new stuff to the game, and we’re expecting to roll out it over the next few months (for ex. [i]expedition mode, chapter 2 & 3, new dinosaurs, AI improvements[/i]), but feel free to continue to leave us feedback, we’re always listening!

[h3]And if you havent yet, please leave a review! This really helps us! Let's get to 200!

notes.title: [0.4.345] Gamepad Patch Release
notes.notes:
Hello, Dino Fans! 

Controller support has arrived. Grab a controller, sit back, and enjoy a whole new way of playing Dino Trauma. You can swap between a controller ([i][b]Playstation[/b][/i] or [i][b]Xbox[/b][/i]) and keyboard & mouse at any time simply by using your desired input method. While both inputs essentially share the same UI, there are a few bespoke elements for each method that will change automatically.

Also, some improvements on visuals, more optimization are made and some minor bugs are fixed.

If you notice any issue or problems with above pls post it on steam forum or our discord. We know that it's still place to improve.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43155973/e0f8c3ee22eb591627c99e2c2439bd71daa369f3.png[/img]
Today, we're bringing you an update focused on fixing some long-standing problems as well as introducing some new additions that we believe you will enjoy!

notes.title: Dino Trauma DevBlog #2
notes.notes:
Last few days have been full of tweaks and adjustments to the level details. The mechanic is currently functional, but it will still need more balancing and more visual effects. There’s also a lot of new 3d assets (laboratory equipment etc.) that need to be set, because it has a relationship to the Lore. 

Yes, there is a story in Dino Trauma. It’s just that it’s not a journey, where you spend a short time in an area, unlock a cutscene and move on to the next area. This is a format that works well in games, but it would not work in our project. First of all our team is too small to focus on that (one programmer and one graphics designer). Second, we want to achieve boomer shooter style, so dynamic and fast environment is our priority.

There’s much more going on but I think I’ll put a pin in it here. Take care and I’ll see you in the next one!

There wasn’t any news from us recently, but that doesn’t mean we halted the development. So first of all thanks to all of you, patiently awaiting the release of Dino Trauma. Your sincere interest in our game invariably gives us strength and motivation to continue working further, and we are very grateful.

Game development is a very complex and stressful process, and sometimes it takes a lot of effort, but 2023 will be super important for us! We would like to release [b][u]Early Access at the end of March[/u][/b], and we have plans to deliver big updates regularly - we will share full roadmap in next few weeks.

However, we still have a lot of work to do. Currently, we focus on:

[i]• level design improvements
• better gunplay experience
• more complex lore and environment interactions
• animations tweaks[/i]
